text:
maria-garcia: Heads-up — several customers reported redwoodctl MSI installer (0.9.2) on Windows 11 fails to persist profile after reboot. Local serve falls back to unauthenticated mode. Anyone seen this?
owen-kim: Noticed that too in the onboarding sandbox. Installer puts config in C:\ProgramData\Redwood\config.json which our runtime refuses to read unless run as admin. The user-level config at %USERPROFILE%\.redwood gets ignored because the GUID-based lookup prefers the ProgramData path.
maria-garcia: reproducible steps for me: install MSI (default), run `redwoodctl login`, see success, reboot, `redwoodctl local serve` logs `WARN no token found, running fallback`.
kevin-wu: can you paste the login output? Might be the credential helper on Windows didn't persist.
maria-garcia: login output: 
```
C:\> redwoodctl login
Open browser to https://auth.redwood.dev/...
Logged in as maria@gdomain.com
Persisting credentials via windows-credential-manager: failed: access denied
Success: session stored in memory only
```
so it shows 'failed: access denied' which explains the reboot loss.
irene: looks like the installer process creates ProgramData dir owned by SYSTEM and the credential helper tries to write a file there rather than invoking the Windows Credential Manager API. That's a bug from an earlier port.
devx-bot: Created ticket devex/cli#4628 "Windows MSI drops to ephemeral session when credential helper write fails" — https://github.com/redwood-inference/devex/issues/4628 :white_check_mark:
owen-kim: temporary workarounds: 1) run `redwoodctl login --token <token>` (explicit token write to %USERPROFILE%/.redwood), 2) reinstall using the ZIP distribution and update PATH manually, or 3) give the user profile write perms to ProgramData\Redwood (not ideal).
kevin-wu: we should change installer to write only default config templates to ProgramData and always resolve per-user config first, then fall back. Also catch credential helper errors and surface instructions instead of silently proceeding. Filing a PR.
maria-garcia: another wrinkle — sample app `todo-sample` uses `redwoodctl local serve --config /etc/redwood/config.json` in docs which is Linux-ism; Windows users copy that and end up pointing to non-existent path. We should add platform-specific quickstarts.
irene: agree. I'm updating the onboarding docs to include Windows and macOS notes and adding an explicit `redwoodctl login --persist` note for Windows.
kevin-wu: opened PR devex/cli#4630 fixes: installer permission handling + better error message when credential helper fails + docs updates. Adding an integration test for Windows CI that runs login then reboot simulation (restart process).
infra-bot: Scheduled staging rollout for redwoodctl 0.9.3-windows-fix on 2026-03-27T05:00:00Z pending QA.
maria-garcia: thanks — for the immediate customer triage I DM'd them the `redwoodctl login --token` method and a short Powershell snippet to persist the token into %USERPROFILE%\.redwood: 
```powershell
$token = Read-Host -Prompt "paste redwood token"
$cfg = @{ profiles = @{ default = @{ token = $token } } ; active_profile = "default" } | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 5
$cfg | Out-File -FilePath $env:USERPROFILE\.redwood\config.json -Encoding utf8
```
kevin-wu: saved — and we'll prioritize a small hotfix. If anyone else sees weird auth-on-reboot reports, ping this thread and include `redwoodctl login --debug` output.
devx-bot: Note: if you need to test local serve without persisting, `redwoodctl serve --token <token>` will bypass config resolution.
maria-garcia: closing the loop — workaround applied for two customers, patch in staging. Appreciated! :pray:
